name: Tumor Necrosis Factor Receptor-Associated Periodic Syndrome

criteria.description: Recurrent febrile episodes lasting >= 7 days (typically 1-4 weeks)
Family history of recurrent febrile episodes
Abdominal pain, pleuritis, arthralgia during episodes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Eurofever criteria: TNFRSF1A pathogenic mutation plus compatible clinical features. Clinical suspicion based on recurrent febrile episodes >7 days duration with migratory rash, periorbital edema, and myalgia.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Autosomal dominant inheritance. Attacks typically last 1-4 weeks (longer than FMF). R92Q and P46L are low-penetrance variants with uncertain pathogenicity.

pathognomonic.notes: Duration distinguishes TRAPS from FMF (1-3 days) and HIDS (3-7 days)
Rash and myalgia migrate centrifugally from proximal to distal

rare.notes: Occurs in ~10% of patients with pathogenic mutations; presents as proteinuria
Monocytic fasciitis underlying the migratory myalgia

laboratory: Elevated ESR, CRP, SAA during attacks
Low soluble TNF receptor 1 levels (impaired shedding) - specialized test
imaging: MRI of affected muscle: fascial edema/enhancement during attacks
genetic: Common pathogenic variants: C33Y, T50M, C88R (cysteine mutations are higher pathogenicity)
R92Q and P46L are low-penetrance/uncertain significance variants
Autosomal dominant inheritance with variable penetrance
other: Skin/muscle biopsy during attack: monocytic/lymphocytic perivascular infiltrate
Response to anti-IL-1 therapy (anakinra, canakinumab) supports diagnosis

distinguishingFeatures: FMF attacks are shorter (1-3 days vs 1-4 weeks in TRAPS)
FMF responds to colchicine; TRAPS does not
AOSD has quotidian fever, salmon rash, markedly elevated ferritin

redFlags: Proteinuria developing in TRAPS patient (AA amyloidosis risk ~10%)
Failure to respond to corticosteroids (may need IL-1 blockade)
Very prolonged attacks (> 6 weeks) suggesting alternative diagnosis
New diagnosis of cysteine-residue mutation (higher amyloidosis risk)
references: Lachmann HJ, et al. Clinical and subclinical inflammation in patients with familial Mediterranean fever and in heterozygous carriers of MEFV mutations. Rheumatology. 2006;45(6):746-750.
Gattorno M, et al. Classification criteria for autoinflammatory recurrent fevers. Ann Rheum Dis. 2019;78(8):1025-1032.
Cudrici C, et al. Revisiting TNF Receptor-Associated Periodic Syndrome (TRAPS): Current Perspectives. Int J Mol Sci. 2020;21(9):3263.
